body:
OBSERVED 2026-09-26 by the independent review of #2313 (code-read, with the renderer bytes measured
in the image): cps/services/koreader_library.py iso_z uses strftime, so a year below 1000 comes
out "101-..." on the image (Python 3.13 glibc) and "0101-..." on macOS and Python 3.14.

It feeds the manifest's `added` field and, through last_modified, `book_rev` / `rev`, as well
as the placeholder EPUB's `modified` (kosync_library.py:237). The plugin's isoToTime accepts
only 4-digit years, so the image's "101-..." never parses, and sorting `added` as a string puts
3-digit years out of order. `revision` excludes `added`, so there is no whole-library churn.

Related sites, where only the output bytes vary per interpreter and nothing is fingerprinted:
- cps/db.py atom_timestamp (the OPDS updated/mtime values)
- cps/templates/feed.xml published (real pubdates before 1000)
- cps/db.py custom datetime columns embedded in downloaded EPUB metadata

Fix shape: format by hand to 4 digits here. Unlike Kobo, the manifest is not fingerprinted by
the server, so the pinned-bytes constraint of #2313 does not apply.
title: KOReader library manifest renders years below 1000 per interpreter and unparseable
